title: Daratumumab-containing vs non-daratumumab-containing regimens for PFS in RRMM
question: In adults with confirmed relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma, do daratumumab-containing regimens versus non-daratumumab-containing regimens improve progression-free survival?
population: Adults (age >=18 years) with a confirmed diagnosis of relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM).
pubmed_queries: daratumumab[tiab] AND "multiple myeloma"[tiab] AND (relapsed[tiab] OR refractory[tiab]) AND ("randomized controlled trial"[pt] OR randomized[tiab] OR randomised[tiab])
eligibility_summary: RCTs in adults with confirmed RRMM comparing daratumumab-containing with non-daratumumab-containing regimens; reporting ORR, CR rate, PFS, or MRD negativity rate. Human studies published in English; pediatric patients and other malignancies excluded.

primary_outcome.name: Progression-free survival
primary_outcome.definition: The length of time from the start of treatment to disease progression or death.
primary_outcome.primary_status: Proposed benchmark outcome; the meta-analysis does not explicitly designate a single primary outcome.

sources: Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials
additional_methods: Manual reference-list searches of identified articles and relevant reviews

benchmark.scope: Open-access meta-analyses whose included trials are all recent (started 2010 or later) and prospectively registered.
benchmark.scope_note: Benchmark selection scope; not an additional eligibility restriction attributed to the comparator meta-analysis.

captain_adjudication.by: captain, 15 Oct 2026 (benchmark build ruled by Dispatch D1 on Mahmood's delegation)
captain_adjudication.primary_outcome: the meta designates no sole primary: the pooled outcome its abstract reports FIRST is used
captain_adjudication.timepoint: each trial's reported analysis as the meta pooled it; no common horizon invented
captain_adjudication.scope: mirrors the meta's own stated eligibility verbatim (a benchmark copies its comparator's PICO)
captain_adjudication.search_window: no date filter on our recorded search; trials published after the meta's search date are reported by the tracker's PUBLISHED_AFTER_COMPARATOR route, never hidden

amendments.by: captain (benchmark build, Dispatch D1 on Mahmood's delegation)
amendments.before_results: yes: only the first draft screen had run (0 of 123 included); nothing extracted or pooled
amendments.reason: the registered screening vocabulary was a paraphrase of the comparator meta's PICO, not screenable terms: population required 'relapsed/refractory' in the title/conditions (POLLUX, CASTOR, APOLLO titles say only 'multiple myeloma'); comparator was the phrase 'non-daratumumab-containing regimens', which no record contains (LEPUS, CANDOR). Add-on trials compare daratumumab + backbone vs the same backbone

amendments.title: Amendment 2 (16 Oct 2026)
amendments.reason: Post-retrieval correction: select the report cited by the comparator using source-derived Table 1/reference identity links; register any-grade harms and controls.
amendments.control_selection_note: Positive controls name the comparator-selected reports, derived through the held Table 1/reference family links. Earlier reports remain companions; the controls still require each selected report to pass screening, rather than relaxing the gate.

g1g2_amendment.harms_policy: Extract held arm-linked cells; refuse unbound tuples with source spans; suppress quantitative synthesis while any reporting row is not extracted.

protocol_ambiguities: PFS is a proposed benchmark focus, not an explicitly designated primary outcome; ORR, CR and MRD negativity are also listed. Captain must adjudicate primary selection.
No common PFS follow-up horizon or analysis population (e.g. intention-to-treat) is specified in the outcome methods; timepoint remains null.
The comparator is defined as non-daratumumab-containing regimens; the methods do not require one particular background regimen.
route_query_note: PubMed fielded Boolean and ctgov cond/intr strings are unexecuted operational translations of the quoted concepts, not verbatim original search strategies. Historical source/date windows are recorded in search_methods; these custom metadata fields are not asserted to enforce retrieval cutoffs. Query syntax and historical-window enforcement require adjudication before any run.
